name: Ad Hominem
shortDef: Attacking the person instead of their argument.
definition: Rejecting a claim because of who makes it (their character, motives, background or track record) instead of engaging with the reasons or evidence they offer.
howToSpot: Is the reply about the person or about the point they made?
Would the rebuttal still work if someone else made the same claim?
Insults, motives or past slip-ups offered in place of counter-evidence
classicExample: Why would we take budget advice from Dev? He can't even keep his own desk tidy.
legitimateVersion: Pointing out a real conflict of interest or a poor track record is fair when a claim rests on someone's word alone, but it's a reason to check the evidence, not to reject the claim.

contrast.fal_tu_quoque: Ad hominem attacks the person's character or motives; tu quoque deflects by saying the critic does the same thing.
contrast.fal_guilt_by_association: Ad hominem targets the person making the claim; guilt by association targets who they're linked with.
contrast.fal_genetic_fallacy: Ad hominem targets the person arguing now; the genetic fallacy dismisses a claim by its origin or history.
